rows.invariant: G2: no path, no claim (a suspect with no causal path is eliminated)
G5: a suspect whose max flow cannot carry the observed impact is eliminated
G1: the cause must have been seen in a graph result of this run
approval is bound to the exact plan hash (choosing ≠ approving)
execute refuses a stored action that no longer matches its approved plan hash
verification that cannot read a channel is UNKNOWN, never success
write-back never records success for an UNKNOWN verification
learned remediation ordering only reorders enabled options (disabled ones never move)
a bystander change is not confirmed when the anomaly shows only at the symptom (G4 origin)
a suspect's own G5 bound counts every failure path (min(1, k × maxFlow)) (impact_bound)
joint G5 eliminates a suspect only when another suspect can carry the impact ALONE (never on the strength of a group whose members are each insufficient: that choice is order-dependent)
a change on the alerting component itself is always a suspect (Q-SUS-1 keeps the symptom row)
every template read goes through GRAPH.RO_QUERY
FAULTLINE_DISABLE_GRAPH=true makes every read fail loudly (ablation arm A4; two guards, both removed)
templates may not contain write clauses
guarded text2cypher rejects write keywords
the brain's citation guard refuses ids no tool call of the question returned
tenant names are validated (no cross-tenant or injected graph names)
G7: a code/data specialist naming another change than the cause downgrades confidence (§6.4)
a tool outside the stage whitelist is refused, logged and recorded (§6.2)
two dispatches of the same specialist work item never both run it (W-CLAIM-1, §6.13): claim_task claims for every caller
alert grouping links two alerts only over edges that can carry an alert-worthy rise (a grouping that joins every edge in the region merges unrelated faults into one incident)
only OPEN incidents absorb new alerts (a resolved incident's origin never attaches one)
a target is a consequence of another alert only when a failure can cross the edges between them (Q-PRIMARY-1 uses the grouping's carry rule)
verification allows the share of a symptom another OPEN incident still owns (without it, S14's real payment fix reads NOT_APPLIED because the concurrent fraud fault still leaks into checkout)
the allowance never covers this incident's own fault (counting its own confirmed origin turns a fix that does not contain it into APPLIED)

the allowance is an upper bound under the telemetry model: the other origin's path transfer over uncut edges (sum of cap products), never the bottleneck max flow over the full topology (which over-states a multi-hop leak and lets a partial fix hide its own residual inside the allowance)

a verdict is written only while its intent is PENDING and leased to the writer (review round 4, M5): an unconditional verdict lets a late reconciler or a stalled execute job overwrite the settled outcome

a data repair is executed and verified on its incident's own warehouse fixture (review round 5, M2): without re-establishing the recorded mode and sources digest, a healthy-mode run in between makes a patch that fixes nothing verify APPLIED
an LLM-authored transform must be one plain CTAS of its own target (review round 5, M4): a validator that accepts anything lets `COPY … TO` write files from the build
brain session ids are server-issued (sess-…) and never take another node's id (review round 4, M1): unprefixed client sessions make a second node with a component's id
each containment candidate's future is read on its own GRAPH.COPY branch with ITS cut edges removed (M14 #1): a branch that keeps them predicts every flag fails, and the plan buries the working lever
learned ordering never lifts an option the futures predict will not contain above one they predict will (history reorders within a predicted-future class only)

a suspect whose whole anomaly an earlier upstream fault accounts for (strict lower bound) is not the origin (deep bench: without the G4 rules a look-alike downstream of an unchanged break was confirmed in 16 of 20 worlds)
elimination takes no slack: a surplus at the suspect may be its own fault (adversarial review: two causes in a chain)
the negative proof requires every alerting symptom to be measured (N0, found by the robustness eval: deleted telemetry was read as 'no incident')
verification's post-action telemetry keeps the world's base error rates (found by the futures eval: re-drawing them from the noise seed read a contained fault as not contained)
who_fixes reads every page of its projection (M14 #6): stopping after the first silently drops the pairs of a busy component, the LIMIT-100 truncation the Cypher move fixed
only an INTENTIONAL reviewer answer takes a decision out of G8 for that change (M15 #3): honouring any answer would let "accidental" or "discuss" silently waive a violation
the graph learns a failure link only from a fix VERIFIED APPLIED (M15 #4): learning from an unverified or failed rollback turns a wrong human guess into a wrong edge
approving a learned link re-checks, in the write itself, that its fix is still APPLIED, the approver is an active person and the graph still has no path (prejudge 2026-10-13)
